question: P, Q and R invested a sum in the ratio of 12 : 82 : 38, respectively. If they earned a total profit of ₹3,510 at the end of year, what is the difference between the shares of Q and R?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time period is the same for all, the profit ratio is equal to the investment ratio.

Ratio of P : Q : R = 12 : 82 : 38 (Total = 132 parts)

Difference in ratio parts of Q and R = 82 − 38 = 44 parts

Required difference = (44 ÷ 132) × Total Profit

Required difference = (1 ÷ 3) × 3510 = ₹1,170

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,170.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of investments of P, Q, and R = 12 : 82 : 38

Total profit earned at the end of the year = ₹3,510

**Formula Used:**

Profit Share ∝ Investment (when time is constant)

Value of a share = (Ratio part of share ÷ Sum of all ratio parts) × Total Profit

 
 Total Profit = ₹3,510 (132 parts)

 Diff = 82 − 38 = 44 parts

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of all profit ratio parts = 12 + 82 + 38 = 132

⇒ Difference in ratio parts of Q and R = 82 − 38 = 44

⇒ Difference in their shares = (Difference in ratio parts ÷ Total ratio parts) × Total Profit

⇒ Difference in amount = (44 ÷ 132) × 3,510

⇒ Difference in amount = (1 ÷ 3) × 3,510

⇒ Difference in amount = ₹1,170

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,170.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When all partners invest their capital for the same time period, the profit is distributed exactly in the ratio of their invested capitals. Formula: Profit Ratio = C₁ : C₂ : C₃.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different time periods, the profit ratio is the product of capital and time. Formula: Profit Ratio = C₁×T₁ : C₂×T₂ : C₃×T₃.

Working and Sleeping Partners

A working partner actively manages the business and receives a fixed salary or a certain percentage of the total profit. The remaining profit is divided among all partners (including the working partner) in the ratio of their investments.
